verdict.rationale: Obsidian stores all notes as plain local Markdown files (obsidian-docs-20, obsidian-docs-23), which lets any script or agent read and write vault content directly on disk without opening the GUI, and Obsidian URI (obsidian-docs-8) lets external processes trigger note-creation/open actions. However, there is no first-party documented REST/MCP server or agent-facing API for note read/write in this evidence — the only official programmatic surface (obsidian-gh-1/2 Vault API) is a plugin API that runs inside the app, and the 'headless' claim (obsidian-docs-10) is scoped to Sync syncing, not note content read/write. Missing for 10: an official first-party MCP server or REST API for note CRUD, and independent hands-on confirmation of agent-driven headless read/write beyond raw file access.
